title: Yudhishthira in hell
hookLine: Yudhishthira reaches heaven, finds his old enemy enthroned there, and goes looking for his family
carry: heaven and hell are stops, not the end
tomorrow: why would God need to be born at all?

cards: The chariot sets him down in heaven, and the first face Yudhishthira sees is Duryodhana's. The cousin behind the rigged game of dice. The man who had Draupadi dragged into the hall.
The one who would not make peace. He sits in splendor, honored among the gods. Yudhishthira's brothers are nowhere.
Draupadi is nowhere. Karna is nowhere. And the man who refused heaven's chariot rather than abandon a dog says, in effect, that he does not want this heaven.
Take me to my brothers. Wherever they are, that's where I want to be.

teach.b: The sage Narada tries to calm him: old quarrels end here, and Duryodhana died fighting as a warrior. Yudhishthira won't be calmed. So the gods send a messenger to guide him to his family.
The path turns dark and smells of decay. Thorns, burning things, a river that scalds. It is a hell.
Yudhishthira turns to go back, and voices call out of the dark. Stay, they beg. While you stand here, a cool breeze blows and our pain eases.
Who are you? Karna, they answer. Bhima.
Dhrishtadyumna. Draupadi. Everyone he loved is in torment, while the man who caused the war sits on a throne.
Yudhishthira is furious, at the gods and at dharma itself.

teach.h: HE CHOOSES TO STAY IN HELL
teach.b: Then he chooses: if his presence comforts them, he will stay in hell. And it ends.
The gods appear, and the darkness lifts. It was an illusion, Indra explains; every king must glimpse hell, and Yudhishthira saw it for his own half-truth in the war, about Drona's son.
He bathes in the heavenly Ganga and finds his family in their true forms. Now the teaching.

teach.h: HEAVEN AND HELL ARE STOPS; THE GOAL IS MOKSHA
teach.b: In Hindu belief, svarga and naraka, heaven and hell, aren't forever. They're places karma passes through. Duryodhana's courage earned him heaven for a time; one half-truth earned Yudhishthira a glimpse of hell.
The Gita says those who reach heaven by merit come back to earth when the merit runs out. The goal beyond both is moksha: freedom.

how: The Svargarohana Parva is the last book of the Mahabharata, heard in recitations of the full epic. Its ending reflects a common Hindu belief: svarga and naraka are temporary, places karma passes through, and the final goal is moksha, freedom from the cycle of rebirth.

o: the heavenly river Ganga where he bathes at the end
heaven, the realm of the gods that Yudhishthira reaches
the hell where Yudhishthira hears his family's voices

games.q: the last book — tap the pairs.

s: Yudhishthira finds his brothers waiting on thrones
he finds Duryodhana enthroned and his brothers apparently in hell.
Yudhishthira decides to stay in hell with his family
he sends the messenger back without him, and then the illusion lifts.
in Hindu belief, heaven is the final goal
svarga lasts only while merit lasts, the Gita says; the goal beyond heaven and hell is moksha.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira. you can go back to heaven's comfort, or stay in a dark place where your presence eases your family's pain. what do you do?
o: stay in the dark with them.
demand the gods bring them up.
games.why: he sends the messenger away and stays, and that choice is what ends the illusion.

practice: This is the end of a very long story, so give it a quiet minute. Think of one person who is going through a hard time right now. Send them a short message, nothing to fix, just that you're thinking of them.
Yudhishthira couldn't end his family's pain; his being there was enough to cool the dark. If you pray, hold them in your prayer as you press send.

wordCard.voice: Svarga. Heaven, the realm Yudhishthira reaches, and then chooses to leave for the hell where his family waits.

orig.note: svarga: heaven, the realm of Indra and the gods, where this book is set.

carryVoice: Hold on to it: heaven and hell are stops, not the end. Tomorrow a new book opens, with a wedding and a sword. That's the end of a very long road.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Svargarohana Parva: Duryodhana in heaven, Narada's counsel, the path to hell, the voices, Yudhishthira's choice, Indra's and Dharma's explanation, the bath in the heavenly Ganga
